subtitle: A Sangam poet walks between spears, ships and kings

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a lone woman on a dusty road between a war-band camp and a distant seaport
panels.action: Avvaiyar of Tagadur stands mid-road, palm-leaf manuscript in hand, warriors on one side and mast-forests of ships on the other, the red earth of Tamil country stretching to the horizon.

dialogue.text: In the age of Sangam, when spears ruled Tamil land, one woman’s verses walked where armies hesitated: Avvaiyar of Tagadur.

i18n.hi: संगम के उस दौर में, जब भाले तमिल भूमि पर राज करते थे, एक औरत के गीत वहाँ पहुँचे जहाँ सेनाएँ भी झिझकीं: टगडूर की अव्‍वैयार।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird’s-eye over a bustling inland town to a close on Avvaiyar walking
panels.action: From above, streets of an early urban Tamil settlement glow with lamps and trade; Avvaiyar moves steadily through the crowd, a cloth bag of palm leaves at her side.

dialogue.text: Her poems are all we have. No birth story, no lineage, only a voice threaded through songs of love and war, speaking from crowded streets like these.

i18n.hi: हमें बस उसकी कविताएँ मिलीं। न जन्म कथा, न वंश, बस एक आवाज़ जो प्रेम और युद्ध के गीतों में गुँथी, ऐसी भीड़भरी गलियों से बोलती।

panels.shot: intimate medium close-up as Avvaiyar pauses by a wall carved with Tamil-Brahmi letters
panels.action: Avvaiyar touches a stone with early Tamil-Brahmi script scratched into it, her fingers tracing the letters as she looks on with a small, knowing smile.

dialogue.text: Keezhadi’s shards and letters tell us of towns, streets, writing. Her verses tell us of the minds that moved through them, weighing kings and fate.

i18n.hi: कीझड़ी के टुकड़े और अक्षर बस्तियों, गलियों, लिखावट की ख़बर देते हैं। उसकी कविताएँ उन दिमागों को दिखाती हैं जो उनमें चलते थे, राजा और किस्मत को तौलते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a rustic assembly where a young Avvaiyar recites to villagers and local fighters
panels.action: Younger Avvaiyar stands under a tree, chanting with raised hand as farmers, herdsmen and lean spear-bearing youths listen, some smiling, some frowning in thought.

dialogue.text: We do not know her childhood. But her early poems already speak to fighters and farmers, turning daily hunger and risk into measured, deliberate words.

i18n.hi: हम उसका बचपन नहीं जानते। पर उसकी शुरुआती कविताएँ ही सिपाहियों और किसानों से बात करती हैं, रोज़ की भूख और ख़तरे को तौले हुए, सोचे-समझे शब्दों में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Tagadur hill-fort with banners fluttering
panels.action: On a rocky hill, the fort of Tagadur rises with wooden palisades and cloth banners; below, horsemen and elephants wait as Avvaiyar approaches the gate.

dialogue.text: One name returns with hers again and again: Athiyaman Neduman Anji of Tagadur, a chieftain in a ring of rival Tamil lords.

i18n.hi: एक नाम बार–बार उसके साथ लौटता है: टगडूर का अथियमन नेडुमन अंजी, प्रतिद्वंद्वी तमिल नायकों के घेरे में एक सरदार।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a timber-pillared hall, Avvaiyar before Athiyaman (implied, off-screen)
panels.action: In a dim wooden hall, Avvaiyar stands poised, palms loosely joined, as unseen warriors sit around, only their spears and ankles visible; her expression is calm yet firm.

dialogue.text: In poems, she praises him not as a mere warlord, but as a giver who feeds bards before battle and restrains his rage for the sake of the land.

i18n.hi: कविताओं में वह उसे न बस जंगी सरदार, बल्कि ऐसा दाता कहती है जो युद्ध से पहले कवियों को खिलाता है, और ज़मीन की ख़ातिर अपने क्रोध को थाम लेता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Avvaiyar’s face lit by firelight as she speaks to Athiyaman seated opposite (only his hands and ornaments visible)
panels.action: Firelight flickers on Avvaiyar’s lined face as she looks across at a pair of jewelled hands resting on a spear, her gaze steady, lips parted mid-verse.

dialogue.speaker: avvaiyar_i
dialogue.text: “Lord, the world calls you great when your anger is delayed, not when your spear is swift.”

i18n.hi: “स्वामी, दुनिया तुम्हें तब महान कहती है जब तुम्हारा ग़ुस्सा ठहरता है, न कि जब भाला तेज़ हो।”

panels.shot: sweeping wide of rival chieftain camps across a valley, with Avvaiyar walking the slope between
panels.action: Two camp clusters face each other across a dry valley, banners of different symbols snapping; Avvaiyar walks a narrow path down the separating slope, alone, robes pressed by wind.

dialogue.text: Her verses name many chiefs. She appears and vanishes between them, a guest moving from one fire to the next, as alliances form and split.

i18n.hi: उसकी कविताओं में कई नायकों के नाम हैं। वह उनके बीच दिखती–ओझल होती है, एक मेहमान जो एक आग से दूसरी आग तक चलती है, जैसे मेल–मिलाप बनते और टूटते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot in a rival chieftain’s tent, Avvaiyar addressing a tense council
panels.action: Inside a tent hung with weapons, a rival chief grips his spear while advisors lean in; Avvaiyar stands just inside the doorway, hand raised in measured appeal.

dialogue.text: In one poem, she warns a hot-headed lord that easy war brings hard famine. Her counsel, framed as praise and proverb, moves where harsh rebuke would be cut down.

i18n.hi: एक कविता में वह एक गर्ममिज़ाज सरदार को चेताती है कि आसान युद्ध कठोर अकाल लाता है। उसकी नसीहत, जो प्रशंसा और कहावत बनकर आई, वहाँ चल गई जहाँ कड़ी डाँट काट दी जाती।

panels.shot: transition shot from inland fort to seaport using a tracking move that follows Avvaiyar’s stride
panels.action: As Avvaiyar walks past the edge of a fort, the scene blends into a busy seaport road, her stride continuous as bullock-carts, pack-men and sailors jostle around her.

dialogue.text: Her poems also know the sea. They speak of ports where foreign ships anchor, of merchants weighing pepper against gold, of roads that bind hill and coast.

i18n.hi: उसकी कविताएँ समंदर को भी जानती हैं। वे उन बंदरगाहों की बात करती हैं जहाँ परदेसी जहाज़ लगते हैं, जहाँ सौदागर काली मिर्च को सोने से तौलते हैं, जहाँ सड़कें पहाड़ और तट को बाँधती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling Sangam seaport with Roman-style ships and Tamil warehouses
panels.action: At a tidal creek, tall-masted ships with unfamiliar rigging lie at anchor; on the wharf, Tamil workers stack jars and bales as Avvaiyar watches, wind whipping her shawl.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists later find Roman coins and amphorae on such coasts. Her lines remember them as living traffic, as chances for lords to share or hoard wealth.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद पुरातत्त्ववेत्ता इन्हीं तटों पर रोमन सिक्के और घड़े खोद निकालते हैं। उसकी पंक्तियाँ उन्हें ज़िंदा आवाजाही की तरह याद रखती हैं, ऐसे मौक़े जिन्हें लेकर नायक दौलत बाँट भी सकते हैं, दबा भी सकते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Avvaiyar speaking with a merchant by piled goods
panels.action: Beside heaps of pepper sacks and fine cloth, Avvaiyar talks with a bearded merchant who clutches a tally-stick, his eyes wary yet attentive.

dialogue.speaker: avvaiyar_i
dialogue.text: “What use your ship’s hold if the road home burns? Tell your lord this, trader.”

i18n.hi: “किस काम का तेरे जहाज़ का कोठा, अगर लौटने वाली राह ही जल जाए? ये अपने स्वामी से कह, व्यापारी।”

panels.shot: medium shot of Avvaiyar at a gift-giving in Athiyaman’s hall, observing with critical eyes
panels.action: In Athiyaman’s hall, warriors receive garlands and gifts; Avvaiyar stands to one side, watching as a poor bard with torn cloth hesitates at the back.

dialogue.text: Many of her Purananuru poems turn on gifts. She praises chiefs who reward the lowly and sharers, and shames the tight-fisted by setting their names beside generous rivals.

i18n.hi: उसकी कई पुरानानूरु कविताएँ दान पर टिकती हैं। वह उन नायकों की सराहना करती है जो ग़रीबों और बाँटने वालों को पुरस्कृत करें, और कंजूसों को यूँ लाज दिलाती है कि उनके नाम औदार्य के प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के साथ रख देती है।

panels.shot: close-up of Avvaiyar composing, scratching on a palm leaf with stylus
panels.action: Seated in a quiet corner, Avvaiyar leans over a palm leaf, stylus in hand, brow furrowed as she presses letters into the smooth surface.

dialogue.text: These were not private diaries. Each poem was a public act, recited, remembered, and only much later written, copied, and woven into anthologies with other voices.

i18n.hi: ये निजी डायरी नहीं थीं। हर कविता एक सार्वजनिक कर्म थी, बोली, याद रखी गई, और बहुत बाद में लिखी, उतारी, और दूसरी आवाज़ों के साथ संकलनों में पिरोई गई।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of different recitation settings dissolving into one another
panels.action: Avvaiyar’s figure appears in a series of overlapping scenes: in a battlefield camp, in a rustic village, in a coastal warehouse, in a court pavilion, always with listeners gathered.

dialogue.text: Narrinai, Kuruntokai, Akananuru, Purananuru: later scholars group her scattered songs under these names, but in her time they were moments, events, spoken into specific rooms.

i18n.hi: नारिनै, कुरुंतोकै, अकानानूरु, पुरानानूरु: बाद के विद्वान उसकी बिखरी रचनाओं को इन नामों के नीचे जोड़ते हैं, पर उसके समय में वे बस पल थे, घटनाएँ, जो ख़ास कमरों में बोल दी जाती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Avvaiyar gently yet firmly rebuking a lord who failed his people
panels.action: In a shaded colonnade, a richly dressed chief looks away, jaw tight, as Avvaiyar stands before him, hand resting on her walking staff, gaze unflinching.

dialogue.text: She does not spare kings. One poem tells a ruler that his people starve while his granaries swell, that fame built on neglect will crumble like mud walls in rain.

i18n.hi: वह राजाओं को भी नहीं बख़्शती। एक कविता में वह शासक से कहती है कि उसकी जनता भूखी है जबकि कोठारें भरी हैं, कि लापरवाही पर बनी शोहरत बारिश में मिट्टी की दीवारों की तरह ढह जाएगी।

panels.shot: close-up on Avvaiyar’s eyes, layered over faint manuscript imagery hinting at later transmission
panels.action: Avvaiyar’s ageing eyes fill the frame, lines at their corners; behind them, faintly, the ghostly image of later palm-leaf manuscripts and careful scribes appears.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scribes in cloisters and courts copy her verses, sometimes debating which Avvaiyar a poem belongs to, arguing over memory even as they preserve it.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, मठों और दरबारों में नकलनवीस उसकी कविताएँ उतारते हैं, कभी यह बहस करते हुए कि कौन–सी कविता किस अव्‍वैयार की है, याद पर झगड़ते हुए भी उसे बचाए रखते हैं।

panels.shot: wide twilight shot of Avvaiyar walking alone on the Sangam road, silhouettes of forts and masts on the horizon
panels.action: At dusk, Avvaiyar walks a lonely road, her figure a dark outline against a horizon where a hill-fort and distant ship masts share the same fading light.

dialogue.text: We do not know where she died, or when. We know instead the road she walked: between rival lords, between hill and sea, between praise and warning.

i18n.hi: हम नहीं जानते वह कहाँ या कब मरी। हम बस यह जानते हैं कि वह कौन–सी राह चली: प्रतिद्वंद्वी नायकों के बीच, पहाड़ और समुद्र के बीच, प्रशंसा और चेतावनी के बीच।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Avvaiyar seated on a rock, reciting to unseen listeners as the landscape around her fades into modern Tamil Nadu
panels.action: Avvaiyar sits on a rock, hand lifted mid-recital; as the view pulls back, the Sangam landscape gently blends into present-day fields, roads and a distant modern town.

dialogue.text: Her life reminds us: a poet’s voice can become a road of its own, carrying counsel across centuries, reaching places where swords, flags and borders should never decide alone.

i18n.hi: उसकी ज़िंदगी याद दिलाती है: कवि की आवाज़ अपनी ही एक सड़क बन सकती है, जो सलाह को सदियों पार ले जाए, वहाँ तक पहुँचे जहाँ तलवारें, झंडे और सरहदें अकेले फ़ैसला न करें।

subtitle_i18n.en: A Sangam poet walks between spears, ships and kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक संगम कवयित्री भालों, जहाज़ों और राजाओं के बीच चलती है
